r: This retry loop pounds the payment gateway like a toddler pressing an elevator button. It makes five attempts at a fixed 200 ms interval, so a 2-second outage uses up every attempt before the upstream recovers. Because one deploy synchronized every client, they retry together and flood the gateway, a thundering herd on a timer. Please switch to exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 10 s, per the AWS architecture guidance) and wrap the call in a circuit breaker. The catch block currently swallows every exception, including 400-series validation errors. It should retry only on 429, 503, and connection resets, because a malformed request will fail the same way on attempt five. The idempotency key header retry logic needs a test; I suspect duplicate charges slip through when the first POST times out but succeeds server-side. Please open a ticket for the metrics gap.
